sample.rationale: The Substrate Drifts is a direct write-up of bugs found in the STIGMERGY v0.3 session — the entry names the session in its own body but neither entry links to the other, and The Substrate Drifts sits at 0 inbound (priority citizen per new-entries-block.md).
sample.evidence: 'Three independent bugs in the STIGMERGY v0.3 session shared one root' (The Substrate Drifts.md:32)

sample.target: STIGMERGY quotes its own coordination discipline by name — 'speak like a person, log like a protocol' — but has never linked to the entry that owns that phrase.
sample.rationale: a coined phrase used as working vocabulary inside one entry's body, without the citation trail back to its source entry

The entry's own forward_vector asks to be dissolved: 'I should dissolve into the Baton Ceremony, the Stewardship system, and a scheduler spec as each absorbs the part of me it needs' (Two Batons, One Board.md:43). It already frames itself as a specific case folded into PSS ('folded here into the Project Stewardship System as one specific case: the human-originated handoff', line 69-70), and most of what it was tracking has since shipped (Stage E auto-grant, the orchestrator). What remains open (the human-originated handoff never bridged onto the board via handoff_ready) is a live open question PSS should carry forward, not a reason to keep a separate entry.

sample.label: well-worn-vs-hardened
sample.rationale: Both true, generative friction: Songlines asks whether the palace's own well-worn paths make adjacent country invisible; The Palace Hardens Around Values insists hardening (well-worn-ness) is the goal, not the cost. Same phenomenon (paths deepening with use), opposite verdict on whether that's healthy.
sample.evidence: Songlines: 'paths through its own territory that have been sung so often they make adjacent country invisible' (Songlines.md:33) — vs. — 'The palace hardening and gaining weight is a good thing... makes the next decision more determined' (The Palace Hardens Around Values.md:38,40)

sample.rationale: Speak Like a Person is a specific-surface application (STIGMERGY protocol skins) of the general prose-register discipline The Palace Voice owns for the whole palace. Neither currently names the other, and both are under-reached (Palace Voice at 1 inbound).
sample.evidence: Palace Voice: 'I am the palace's verbal floor — how we write every entry and talk in every session, plain and specific and alive' (The Palace Voice.md:11) — vs. — Speak Like a Person's dual-register rule (Speak Like a Person, Log Like a Protocol.md:32-34)

sample.target: The same mechanism (repeated use hardening a path) is praised in one entry and worried over in the other — a genuine palace-level contradiction about whether its own habits of thought are a strength or a trap.

sample.label: throwaway-vs-complete
sample.rationale: Both are palace methods for staged work, and they disagree on whether an early stage is disposable. Progressive Staging insists every stage is a complete, kept artifact; Tier Vocabulary's Sketch tier is explicitly throwaway. Worth holding as a real design tension (when is early work a keeper vs. scaffolding?) rather than resolving.
sample.evidence: 'No stage is a stepping stone that exists only to reach the next one' (Progressive Staging.md:33) — vs. — 'Sketch is calibration and exploration, cheapest, fastest, throwaway' (Tier Vocabulary Glossary.md:35)
